name: North Macedonia

income_tax.summary: Flat 10% personal income tax on most income, including employment and self-employment, and residents are taxed on worldwide income. Employee contributions total 28.0% (pension 18.8%, health 7.5%, employment 1.2%, additional health 0.5%).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Best-available value, still unconfirmed for the self-employed: the Public Revenue Office (UJP) publishes one set of social contribution rates (pension 18.8%, health 7.5%, unemployment 1.2%, injury 0.5%; its table covers 2020-2021 and does not say who pays) and PwC gives the employee total as 28.0%. Neither page states a separate self-employed rate or base, so 28% is used as the likely statutory total and flagged low confidence. The base is between 50% and 16 times the average salary (PwC; MKD amounts not found).
income_tax.local_tax_note: PwC does not state personal allowances; the personal allowance is left at zero.

open_questions: Self-employed contribution rate and base not found on any page opened; 28% (the same statutory set of rates) is a best estimate.
Personal allowance and average salary (MKD) not found.
PwC dates the 10% flat rate from 2023; no 2026 change confirmed.

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Average 2026 rent for a 1-bedroom in Skopje per LifeIndexed (method not described).

costs.notes: LifeIndexed lists only 1-bedroom (EUR 374) and 3-bedroom (EUR 695) rents and does not describe its method. Investropa and Expatistan 2-bed pages could not be opened (404, 403). 2-bedroom left null.

residence_routes: No dedicated digital nomad category was found. Search results (law firms, guides) say remote workers typically use a long-stay visa and temporary residence on a business or employment ground; amendments to the Law on Foreigners took effect on 26 September 2025 and simplified documents for employment-based permits. Not verified on an official page.
open_questions: Nomad visa absence rests on secondary sources (search results), not an official page.
